newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 28.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai presson Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A full cabinet list has been submitted to Prime Minister-designat Chavalit Yongchaiyudh and nominees' qualifications are being considered by cabinet secretary-general Visanu Krua-ngarm. New Aspiration secretary-general Sanoh Thienthong has said all except three of the 49 nominees are elected to the House of Representatives. (BANGKOK POST)

- Six suspected drug traffickers have been shot dead after surrendering to police following a 20-hour hostage drama in Suphan Buri province. Police said the suspects were killed because they tried to fight back after their surrender. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- Civic groups that supported Chavalit Yonchaiyudh in the election are to present the first challenge to the new prime minister. Thousands of protestors, mostly farmers, are expected to converge on Bangkok to remind the New Aspiration Party leader to deliver on his election promises on the day his cabinet atkes office. (BANGKOK POST)

- Japan's giant petrochemical producer Mitsubishi Rayon Co has selected Siam Cement Group and Bangkok Synthetics Co as partners in its first project outside Japan to produce methyl methacrylate (MMA). With an investment of three billion baht, the joint venture plant will manufacture 70,000 tonnes of MMA a year for Thailand and other Southeast Asian countries. (THE NATION) (BANGKOK POST)

- Bank of Thailand governor Rerngchai Marakanond has summoned the top executives of five largest local commercial banks for a meeting and asked them to cut interest rates by next week to help jump-start the economy. He told the executives that he expected them to cut their lending rates by at least 25 basis points. (THE NATION)

- Thai Airways International's (THAI) plan to buy 21 airliners for 143 billion baht has won approval from the National Economic and Social Development Board (NESDB). The board has pledged it would support THAI's proposal for consideration by the cabinet. (BANGKOK POST)
